track.label: ACTIVE TRACK
track.title: DRAGONBYTE Z BUILDOUT
track.blurb: Every capability below is a user-facing editor surface or an authoring operation reachable from DragonByte Z itself. A reverse-engineering result is not counted here, however complete it is: knowing a binary structure is not the same as an author being able to use it.

families.label: READ
families.title: Inspect what the game already contains

families.label: AUTHOR
families.title: Create what did not exist before

families.label: DELIVER
families.title: Build it, save it, keep it safe

capabilities.title: Desktop application shell
capabilities.detail: The 4 primary editors are named on one compact strip - Atlas, Inspector, Maps, Graphics - with Open ROM, Open Project, Validate, Build and Run beside them. The Maps editor holds its own Browse, Layout, Objects and Warps modes, the Scene editor is opened from the placement it belongs to, and Build and Run open as dialogs. A loaded image must match a configured profile identity before its content is editable.
limits: The editors are always selectable; with no image loaded each shows its own empty state rather than content.
The loaded image must match a configured profile identity before its content is usable.

The strip is a fixed contract of 4 primary editors with the project actions beside them. Build, Run and the Scene editor are reached as an action or from the placement they belong to, not as permanent destinations.
capabilities.surface: DragonByte Z window: one compact strip naming the Atlas, Inspector, Maps and Graphics editors, with Open ROM, Open Project, Validate, Build and Run beside them, and the Maps editor's Browse, Layout, Objects and Warps modes

capabilities.title: Full-ROM atlas search
capabilities.detail: Search the whole game by name, map or id, including text the game keeps compressed, without knowing a ROM address.
limits: Search is a lookup over the structures the SDK has classified, not a blind byte scan.
Text found inside a compressed container is reported at a derived offset into the decoded stream, which is not a ROM address and is not claimed as a string boundary.
capabilities.surface: Atlas editor: full-ROM search over the game's indexed structures

capabilities.title: Recovered-record inspector
capabilities.detail: Read the fields the SDK has actually recovered for a search result, shown under the names the evidence supports rather than a plausible guess.
limits: Only fields the SDK has actually recovered are shown, under evidence-supported names.
A search result the SDK cannot map is read-only and has no address- or text-based fallback.
capabilities.surface: Inspector editor: recovered-field view of a selected search result

capabilities.title: Sprite, animation and palette browsing
capabilities.detail: See the game's decoded sprites, step their animations, and read which records refer to each one.
limits: The browser draws one piece per direction slot; compositing one frame's pieces into a single image is not built.
Placement-to-sprite identity is not proven, so browsing does not resolve which sprite a map object uses.
capabilities.surface: Graphics editor: sprite, animation and palette browser

capabilities.title: Map browsing: every map and layer
capabilities.detail: All 452 maps render from immutable ROM bytes, layer by layer, at zoom. The selected map's id and name are carried by the map list and the status line, and its extent and each layer's own classification are read back in the Maps editor's Layout mode.
limits: Read-only until the Maps editor's Layout mode is switched on.
Maps and layers outside the proven render form are shown read-only with the reason stated.
A reopened derivative renders its edited layout from reconstructed canonical bytes and stays read-only.
capabilities.surface: Maps editor, Browse mode: read-only layered map view over the map list

capabilities.title: Dialogue line editing
capabilities.detail: Resolve a supported line, edit it, validate and build. A rewritten ordinary NPC line has been displayed by the retail engine in its own dialogue box, and a line may now change decoded length instead of having to match the one it replaces: a longer replacement has been displayed in full, from a record whose durable handle the build re-authored.
limits: Only a line the SDK can resolve as a mapped target is editable; other search results stay read-only.

A line longer than the record it replaces re-authors that record's durable handle and re-lays out its decoded container, so every record after it moves inside the container; a container whose records cross the edited one is refused rather than reinterpreted.

The rebuilt container must stay inside the toolkit's 64 KiB decoded-container limit, which a retail dialogue container nearly fills: this target's ceiling is a 94-byte line, well below the 4,094 bytes the handle's length field can encode.
One record at a time. The SDK's registered dialogue targets hold a single record, and two records in one container would need an explicit batch re-layout.

The longer line is runtime-observed: the retail dialogue box displays the complete authored line, wrapped across two lines by the engine, from a record whose durable handle and decoded length were re-authored at build time.
capabilities.surface: Inspector editor: mapped dialogue line editing, emitted through the Build action

capabilities.title: Shared palette recolour
capabilities.detail: Recolour a shared object palette entry through the project; the SDK owns RGB-to-GBA-word packing and applies it at build.
limits: One shared palette entry at a time, applied at build: there is no arbitrary graphics replacement.
Proven at the emitted-ROM level by rendering the built image; an emulator run of the recolour was not performed.
capabilities.surface: Graphics editor: shared palette entry recolour through the project

capabilities.title: Object placement on the rendered map
capabilities.detail: Select, add and move supported objects directly on the real map, then build and play the result in the original engine.
limits: Supported object types only; unsupported placements render read-only.
Markers are neutral because placement-to-sprite identity is not proven.
Movement uses the proven signed map-pixel contract with an explicit signed-16 range guard.
capabilities.surface: Maps editor, Objects mode: visual placement select, add and move on the rendered map

capabilities.title: Map layout editing: chunk-cell replacement
capabilities.detail: Reassign one 256x256 chunk cell of a map's dominant layer to another chunk that layer already uses. 341 of the 452 maps expose an editable layer; the remaining 111 are read-only, with the reason stated.
limits: One operation only: reassign an existing same-layer dominant-layer chunk cell. The replacement must be a non-null chunk that the same layer already uses elsewhere.
Cell replacement stays an in-place edit of a supported dominant layer: it does not relocate a layer's record, and it accepts no arbitrary map format.
111 of the 452 maps are read-only: dominant grids that use a single chunk, absent dominant layers, and maps outside the proven form state the reason.
Emulator validation of the layout write itself was not performed; the application round-trip, which reopens its own emitted ROM through the manifest it wrote, was.
capabilities.surface: Maps editor, Layout mode: chunk-cell replacement with a same-layer chunk chooser

capabilities.title: Tile painting
capabilities.surface: Maps editor, Layout mode: pick an existing chunk of the layer, then click or drag it onto 256x256 chunk cells
capabilities.detail: Paint the visible layout of an existing supported map: choose one of the chunks a dominant layer already uses, then click or drag to place it in a 256x256 chunk cell. Painting runs through the project as semantic cell edits, so a painted map is saved and reopened like any other authored content, and a build merges the edits into the one write plan. Undo, redo and eyedropper are on one history, a stroke is one undoable gesture, and a paint that changes nothing leaves no history. Proven in the retail engine: after walking out of the area and back in, the authored chunk is what Buu's Fury draws.
limits: The editable unit is the engine's own: one four-byte chunk-cell reference to an existing 256x256 chunk. It is not an individual 8x8 hardware tile, and no surface pretends otherwise.

A cell may only be given a chunk the same layer already uses at another of its cells, so a layer that uses a single chunk has nothing to paint with and is read-only. Creating a chunk the layer does not already use is the separate Chunk creation capability.
No new-map creation, no graphics import and no collision editing. Resizing remains growth only, so painting cannot reshape a map either.
Screen-entry layers, terrain-field layers (Map 19), absent slots and zero-dimension grids are refused with a stated reason rather than forced into a grid they do not have.
Painting does not allocate or relocate: the replacement is a fixed four-byte in-place write, so a build changes only the painted cells.

capabilities.title: Chunk creation and editing
capabilities.surface: Maps editor, Layout mode: Create Chunk from a layer's existing chunk, then paint the new chunk's 32x32 screen-entry plane and use it as a map brush
capabilities.detail: Create a map chunk that did not exist before. Duplicate one of the chunks a dominant layer already draws, rearrange its 32x32 plane of screen entries using only entries that same layer already displays, and save it as a project-owned resource with its own identity. The new chunk then appears in the layer's brush vocabulary, so a map cell can be painted with it, and a build materializes it through the production allocator and resolves the cell to that address. Proven in the retail engine: after walking out of the area and back in, the engine's own loaded BG1 tilemap carries the authored arrangement while BG0, BG2 and BG3 stay byte-identical, and the new body is read from above the original ROM's end.
limits: An authored chunk is a new arrangement of graphics the layer already draws. It adds no tiles, no palettes and no imported artwork; an entry outside the layer's own vocabulary is refused. The chunk editor offers exactly the screen entries the template's layer already displays, which for Grand Kai's BG1 is 104 of them.

A chunk is map-scoped. Its plane holds tile ordinals, which only resolve through the assembled character block of the map it was composed against, so it is composed against one map and placed only in that map's layers, which may be any of them.

The chunk container is emitted in the one kind every canonical chunk uses, so this is not an engine-format experiment, but the format is not re-opened either: a chunk is still a 32x32 plane of 16-bit screen entries and nothing else.
No new-map creation, no graphics import and no collision editing. Chunks stay map-scoped, so a chunk composed against one map is not reusable in another.

The authored body must go above the original ROM end: the canonical image's only declared free region is 256 bytes and a chunk container is larger, so this capability depends on generated expansion rather than fitting in place.

capabilities.title: Map resizing and layer changes
capabilities.surface: Maps editor, Layout mode's structure section: grow a supported layer's chunk grid from the resize form, and create a supported layer into an unused layer slot from the layer list
capabilities.detail: Change the structure of an existing supported map rather than the cells inside it. Grow a supported dominant layer's chunk grid - the resize is top-left anchored, so every existing cell keeps its coordinate and only the cells the growth adds are initialized, from a chunk that same layer already draws or from one the project itself authored. The layer record is re-emitted whole above the original ROM's end and the map's own layer-slot pointer is repointed at it. The engine clamps its camera to the map's declared extent, so a grow also raises that word; the added area is unreachable otherwise. Separately, activate one of a map's four fixed layer slots with a new supported visual layer, then paint its cells with the same brush vocabulary. Proven in the retail engine: after leaving and re-entering the map, the engine's own loaded layer record holds the grown grid and the authored cell, and the added region is displayed at a camera position the retail clamp cannot reach.
limits: Supported layers are the ordinary dominant chunk-grid form, the form 1,516 of the canonical image's 1,808 layer slots use. Screen-entry layers, the terrain-field form Map 19 uses, unused slots and zero-dimension records are refused with their own reason rather than forced into a grid they do not have.

This is controlled growth. A resize may only make a supported layer's grid larger; shrinking is refused, because the references of the cells it would remove have not been shown to be safe to drop. The capability is map growth plus supported layer authoring, not arbitrary bidirectional resizing.

The engine's layer count is fixed at four, because a map root carries exactly four layer-slot pointers. Creating a layer therefore means activating a slot the game leaves unused, which is what the engine actually does; there is no dynamic layer list.

A new layer is a supported visual dominant layer composed from graphics a layer on that same map already draws. It adds no tiles, palettes or imported artwork, and an entry outside that vocabulary is refused. Authored layers and authored chunks are map-scoped.
A map whose definition is shared with another map is refused outright: the root holds the layer-slot pointers and the extent, so editing one would silently change every map that shares it.

No collision authoring, no new-map creation and no graphics import. A grown area is not connected to any transition by this capability: it does not have to be connected to anything, and this surface does not connect it.

The authored record must go above the original ROM's end: the canonical image declares one 256-byte free region and a record grows with the authored grid, so this depends on generated expansion rather than fitting in place.

capabilities.title: Warp and connection editing
capabilities.surface: Maps editor: the Warps mode lists a map's connections and retargets a selected transition's destination, arrival and facing, with Apply and Revert on the editor's own undo history, and the Create transition form authors a transition the image does not contain; on the map itself every supported transition is drawn as its trigger region, a click selects that connection and a drag moves the region as one undoable gesture
capabilities.detail: Read, retarget and create the transitions that carry a player from one area to another. The Warps mode lists the connections of the displayed map as rows and retargets a selected one's destination, arrival position and facing, staged through the project and written by Apply or discarded by Revert, one edit per undo entry. The Create transition form authors a transition the image does not contain: it takes a durable authored identity of the form map:NNNN/transition:<name>, composes the new 24-byte record over a same-map template from the 566-class family - the class 566 of the 735 records use - and the build emits it with an expanded record-pointer array above the original ROM's end, deterministically. All 735 transition records read with no anomalies and round-trip byte-exactly. The map canvas draws every supported transition of the displayed map as its trigger region, a click selects that connection in the Warps list, and dragging the region moves it as a single undoable gesture. Proven in the retail engine: a human-operated mGBA run consumed an authored transition, and the engine's own loaded record array held the authored entry above the original image's end.
limits: The 169-class transition family is refused for retargeting and for creation: its stored arrival is a scene-relative delta the engine composes at run time, not a point, so no safe arrival can be stated for it.
A map whose connection root is shared with another map is refused, because the record array is shared and editing it would change the other map's transitions as well.
An unsupported transition form fails closed with its reason stated rather than being forced into a form the engine does not read.
Record bytes whose meaning is unresolved are preserved and are not editable: +0x13, and the low nibble of +0x10, whose semantics remain unresolved.
The arrival-facing selector 0x03001A34 read zero on every sample of the runtime run, so what it selects is unresolved and its non-zero case is untested.
There is no transition deletion: Revert discards a staged creation, but a saved transition cannot be removed from the project or from the image.

A stale staged creation that a project change has shadowed has no per-row discard action. Apply refuses, nothing is written, both values survive, the conflict is visible, and replacing the session clears it.
A transition the project creates has no record in the image, so its region is drawn read-only on the map canvas and its drag refuses with the reason stated.
This is the supported, proven authoring surface, not every engine transition form.
capabilities.evidence: MAP-WARPS-AND-CONNECTIONS-001; MAP-WARP-FORMAT-001; MAP-WARP-WORKBENCH-001; MAP-WARP-WORKBENCH-RUNTIME-001; MAP-WARP-CREATE-PROJECT-001; MAP-WARP-CREATE-RUNTIME-001; MAP-WARP-CANVAS-001; docs/research/MAP_WARPS_AND_CONNECTIONS.md

capabilities.title: Authored entities and placements
capabilities.detail: Clone and configure an entity that is not present in the original map data; the map's newly created object slot resolves to the authored body.
limits: An authored entity is built from a supported existing type, cloned and configured; no new record format is invented.
Only placement types the SDK has classified can be authored.
capabilities.surface: Maps editor, Objects mode: clone and configure an authored entity and placement

capabilities.title: Authored behavior and scripts
capabilities.detail: Give an authored entity an author-written script and tie it to a deliberate gameplay trigger; the original engine has executed the authored bytes and rendered the result on screen.
limits: Behavior runs through the engine's own dispatch, so an authored trigger is limited to the triggers the engine already offers.
The proven effect path invokes an existing native handler; no new engine operation is added.
capabilities.surface: Maps editor, Objects mode: authored behavior and script on an authored entity

capabilities.title: Authored text beyond the retail slot
capabilities.detail: A line longer than the one it replaces is placed in verified writable space and the owning table entry is repointed, so the engine renders the whole authored message. New text-table ids are not claimed.
limits: An existing text id is rewritten; creating entirely new text-table ids is not claimed.
Relocation is gated per table by declared capability and per entry by measured single-reference ownership, so an entry carrying a second reference is refused.
Storage length is no longer the limit, but display width still is: a long line drawn centred in a large font runs past the edges of the screen.
capabilities.surface: Project workflow: author text/strings.toml, validate, build (or the `webfoot text set` one-off image edit)

capabilities.title: Graphics replacement and import
capabilities.detail: An extracted sprite asset's PNG can be edited in the project and rebuilt, and the retail engine renders the authored pixels - whether the re-encoded payload still fits the slot the original occupied or has to be placed above the original end of the image.
limits: Same dimensions only: the pixel contents may change; the dimensions, the frame layout and the sprite topology may not.
Actor-sprite graphics only. Map chunks, tilesets, UI, HUD and portrait graphics have their own formats and are not covered.
Every confirmed reference to a relocated payload is rewritten, but the published reference set is not claimed to be every word in the image that names that payload.

The re-encoder is not competitive, so an edit whose payload no longer fits its original slot is placed elsewhere by the allocator: in trusted canonical free space when one can host it, and otherwise above the original end of the image, where the build emits a 16 MiB image. Only the expanded case has been proven in the running engine.
No editor surface edits pixels yet. The supported workflow is extract, edit the extracted PNG, validate, build.
capabilities.surface: Project workflow: extract, edit an extracted sprite PNG, validate, build

capabilities.title: New sprite, animation and frame authoring
capabilities.detail: A new actor-sprite identity can be created from DragonByte Z: choose the donor whose proven composition shape every frame keeps, name the sheet each animation slot draws from, choose the existing object slot the appended actor starts its behaviour from, and write sprites/sprites.toml. The document validates and builds through the ordinary project route, and it authors the same identity and actor the retail engine was observed resolving and drawing (SPRITE-NEW-ATTACHMENT-RUNTIME-PARITY-001).
limits: Every authored frame copies the donor's own first frame, so the frame-composition budget is unchanged rather than modelled; a sheet cell that is not exactly the donor's proven rect is refused.
One identity per image, because an appended identity grows the character registry and repoints the two words that name it.
No piece or OAM composition, piece count, tile index or frame geometry is authorable, and no frame timing or delay is: the document has no field for any of them.
The engine's four direction slots are written in sheet order and their screen meaning is unresolved project-wide.

The surface refuses every field-level problem in the values it authors - donor admissibility, sheet form and cell geometry, template resolution, coordinates and the wander box - and carries the two header words it does not author, whose meaning is unresolved.

The surface's carried data-pointer word is the chosen template slot's own, and the recorded runtime document used a neighbouring sibling slot's value 16 bytes higher, so the two documents are not byte-identical and the engine observation is evidence for the mechanism rather than for this exact document.

The rest of the plan - the palette claim checked against the decoded graphics, the allocation and the relocation census - runs at Validate and Build, which report the same refusals with the same text.

A new actor cannot share a map with other map-level authoring: a map receiving an authored placement expansion and a new actor is refused because both re-emit the map's object array, and a map whose record fields are edited is refused because the actor's own plan emits that record and would drop the field edit. A map already declaring 255 object slots cannot take another actor either, because the slot count is one byte.
capabilities.surface: Workbench: Graphics tab, Authored sprite - New, Edit and Remove write sprites/sprites.toml

capabilities.title: New appearance definitions
capabilities.detail: An author creates a new appearance definition in the Graphics tab, and the build writes it as a record appended above the original end of the image. The engine resolves it: a driven session on the final build watched the retail search return an authored record at a post-canonical index for a retail actor, and the Scouter's own character screen then displayed the authored data for that actor - an object whose retail record reads "Fighter" and "This is a martial artist from the Other World" showed the authored name "Goku" and the authored description instead. Growth is by re-emission: the record count is three compiled loop bounds rather than a stored number, so the build moves the whole table above the image's end and rewrites the five literal words and three count bounds that reach it. The roster structure the engine builds from the seen flags is relocated with it, so all twenty-nine compiled statements of its layout are restated for the supported maximum of 240 records.
limits: Not observed on the final opt-in build: the post-canonical seen-flag write. The message path that returns an appended record appends the resolved index to a list rather than constructing the appearance object, so that flag is written by a later step, and the session that reached the resolver ended before it. The flag write was observed previously for the same post-canonical record shape, on a build whose appended record is byte-identical in everything the engine reads; that stands as supporting evidence and is not claimed as re-observed here.

Not observed in ordinary play: the roster display-list builder at 0x08024F3C executing. It has one caller, reached indirectly, and no session reached it. Its layout is statically and review-proven for the supported count of 240, and a build that would exceed that count is refused rather than written.

Taking over a sprite id a canonical record already selects is an explicit, default-off choice per definition, because the engine's search returns an appended record before the retail one and the lookup would be redirected. The surface states the consequence and the build refuses a takeover that was not asked for. Ids a negative-stat record selects can never be taken over and are refused outright.
The record count is stated by three compiled `cmp rN,#0xE8` loop bounds and there is no terminator, so growth means re-emitting the whole table, not appending in place.
The engine keeps one seen bit per record in a 232-bit array, and the block's own initializer zeroes a word two bytes after it, so at most 8 records may be added to the 232 the image has.
An authored definition shares an existing on-screen name, because creating new text-table ids is not shipped for any capability.
capabilities.surface: Workbench: Graphics tab, Authored appearance - New, Edit and Remove write the project's appearance definitions

capabilities.title: New map and scene materialisation
capabilities.detail: A project authors a map identity the image does not contain. The Maps editor's New map action records a durable name, a donor map and the engine's own two-byte key; the build re-emits the whole map table above the original end of the image with the authored row appended, repoints the one word the engine's key lookup loads and raises the one compiled row bound, and gives the new row its own selector word, its own root and its own layer record. A retail map's existing door can then be pointed at it, and the retail engine loads the new map: a person-driven session, watched by a read-only observer that records the engine's own state, saw the active-MapEntry row become index 452 with the authored key, twice, and the player walk in and back out.
limits: The map table carries no count word and no terminator. The row bound is the two instructions of the engine's own helper at 0x080125E0, so growth is a patch of that immediate plus a repoint of the one literal-pool word the key lookup loads at 0x08008A58, not a data edit. At most 58 rows can be appended before a second instruction would have to change; a project past that is refused rather than written.

A created transition whose trigger region overlaps a retail record's own region did not fire in an observed run: the engine keeps every record's trigger live and the retail record took the player instead. Point a supported door at the new map, or author a region no retail record covers.

An authored map inherits its donor's record fields, root, layer records and chunk bodies, so it draws and collides as the donor does. No shipped surface authors a map root's unresolved fields, a new map's on-screen name, or new tiles for it.

The authored row is reached through the project. A reader that reads the map table from the profile still reads the canonical rows, which are retained verbatim, so a retail row is still answered correctly and a built derivative is not re-extracted.

An authored row's table index is its position in name order, and a transition stores map:NNNN, so adding, removing or renaming an authored map moves the rows after it. A change that would move an index a transition already names is refused by name rather than silently re-pointing that door; a hand edit of maps/authored.toml is outside that guard.

Every MapEntry write the build plans stays visible in the moved table, because the map domain runs after every other domain that writes one. An undo or redo of a new-map gesture that the re-index guard refuses leaves the project file correct but the editor's undo history one step out of step, which the surface reports rather than hides.
A savestate written on the canonical image restores a canonical-era MapEntry pointer, so the first rows of such a capture name a retail row until the engine's next transition.
capabilities.surface: Maps editor: New map authors a new map identity; the Warps editor offers authored maps as transition destinations

capabilities.title: Deterministic validate and build
capabilities.detail: A project validates before it builds, repeated builds are byte-identical, and the Build action refuses to write over the source image.
limits: The Build action refuses to write over the source image.
Editing a project invalidates earlier validation and build state, so Build requires Validate again.
capabilities.surface: Build and Validation Report: Validate and Build over the project

capabilities.title: Safe Save As to a new file
capabilities.detail: The output image and its provenance document are built at temporary sibling paths and verified there, so a failed emit or verification leaves an existing destination byte-for-byte intact.
limits: Save As writes a new file; the source image is never written.
The image and its manifest are staged at temporary sibling paths and verified before the destination is replaced.
Every path a save touches is refused against the source.
capabilities.surface: Maps editor Save As New ROM…: emit a new ROM plus its provenance manifest

capabilities.title: Derivative provenance and reopen
capabilities.detail: Save As writes a manifest beside the ROM, and the application reopens its own emitted ROM only when that manifest proves the image is the canonical ROM plus exactly the declared, legal edits. Everything else is refused with the reason stated.
limits: Only an image this feature emitted, with a manifest that matches it, reopens; anything else is refused with the reason stated.
A reopened derivative is browseable and read-only, because further editing belongs to the canonical image it derives from.
Only declared, policy-legal edit classes are accepted, and the canonical image itself is still accepted by identity before any manifest is consulted.
capabilities.surface: Atlas editor ROM open: provenance-checked acceptance of an emitted derivative

capabilities.title: Launch the build in an emulator
capabilities.detail: Run the generated ROM from the same window to check the change in context, without leaving the editor.
limits: Launch starts a configured emulator with the emitted ROM; the editor does not observe or validate the running game.
The emulator is a local setting, so launch is only as reproducible as that configuration.
capabilities.surface: Run action: run the emitted ROM in a configured emulator

researchOnly.statement: A dominant layer's layout cell is a four-byte chunk-pointer field in a fixed-size, in-place record, and redirecting it to another same-layer chunk changes exactly two ROM bytes.
researchOnly.doesNotConfer: It does not make tile painting, new chunks, resizing, relocation or arbitrary map formats available; the shipped editor performs exactly one operation.

researchOnly.statement: The actor sprite frame record is an 8-byte header with 12-byte pieces carrying their stored pixel extents, and the frame header equals its pieces' bounding box on every frame.
researchOnly.doesNotConfer: It does not ship sprite, animation or frame authoring, nor graphics import: those still need allocation and a production replacement path.

researchOnly.statement: Every reachable canonical container decodes byte- and extent-identically, and the decoder refuses a malformed stream instead of clipping it into a success.
researchOnly.doesNotConfer: It does not ship a packed-container encoder, so a container whose payload changes size still cannot be rewritten in place.

researchOnly.statement: A placement's stored signed position halfwords copy exactly into the actor's Q8 coordinate fields, making signed low-halfword X and high-halfword Y map pixels the reversible authoring contract.
researchOnly.doesNotConfer: It does not ship new maps or map-root authoring.

researchOnly.statement: All 735 transition records read with no anomalies and the record layout is confirmed.
researchOnly.doesNotConfer: Knowing the record layout does not ship warp editing by itself: the shipped capability also needed the project write path, an editor surface and a runtime proof of an authored transition.
